entries.title: Seitz spatial operation
entries.definition: Combines a rotation or reflection with a fractional translation into a spatial operation. The operation on the right acts first.

variables.meaning: Integer rotation matrix in direct-lattice fractional coordinates

entries.conventions: multiplies to {R|t}{S|u}={RS|Ru+t}; fractional coordinates is not equal to Cartesian coordinates .
entries.conditions: Use the same cell, origin, and coordinate conventions before comparing sources.

entries.title: Hermann–Mauguin crystallographic group symbols
entries.definition: Crystallographic symbols specify the lattice type and the rotation, screw, and mirror components arranged along designated directions.

variables.meaning: Twofold screw: a twofold rotation combined with a half-period translation

entries.conventions: The overbar belongs to the corresponding rotoinversion numeral; a screw-axis subscript specifies its fractional translation.
entries.conditions: Read the symbol together with its setting. An arbitrary string of digits cannot automatically be split into screw-axis subscripts.

entries.title: Character of a representation
entries.definition: The trace of a representation matrix, used for decomposition and consistency checks within a conjugacy class or an appropriate projective convention.

variables.meaning: Matrix representing a group element in the state space

entries.conventions: χ(E) is equal to representation dimension ; the same character table must use a consistent order of operations and factor system.
entries.conditions: An antiunitary operation cannot be treated as an ordinary linear matrix whose trace is inserted into unitary-character orthogonality formulas.

entries.title: Irreducible representations and decomposition multiplicities
entries.definition: irreducible representation is a subspace that cannot be decomposed under the action of the selected group; multiplicity represents the number of copies it appears.
entries.conventions: This site's D1, D2, etc. are usually local numbers calculated this time and are not automatically equal to the BC/Bilbao label.
entries.conditions: Check that multiplicities are nonnegative integers, that the characters are reconstructed, and that the total dimension is conserved.

entries.title: Little groups and momentum stars
entries.definition: The little group preserves a selected wavevector modulo reciprocal-lattice vectors; its momentum star collects the distinct images under the full group.

variables.unit: See the coordinate convention of the current module

variables.meaning: Space-group subgroup that leaves k invariant

entries.conventions: A spatial point operation acts on the wavevector as R⁻ᵀk; an antiunitary operation introduces an additional minus sign.
entries.conditions: Little-group representations, induction over the full k star, and induction from real-space sites are distinct constructions.

entries.title: Translation mismatches and projective factor systems
entries.definition: An extra lattice translation in a product of Seitz representatives becomes a phase factor in the representation at fixed k.

variables.meaning: Lattice vector between the product of representatives and the chosen representative
Complex phase in the multiplication law

entries.conventions: The non-spin unitary case has U_gU_h=exp(−2πik·Δ_gh)U_j.
entries.conditions: Spinorial double-valued and antiunitary cases also require the appropriate signs and complex-conjugation rules.

entries.title: Double groups and 2π rotations
entries.definition: introduces a central element to record the sign of a spinor under 2π rotation, making single values ​​and double-valued representation tractable in a group framework.

variables.meaning: Central element corresponding to a 2π rotation in the double group

entries.conventions: Interpret a double-group overbar using the convention for its specific element; it is different from the overbar on an HM rotoinversion axis.
entries.conditions: Describes spatial rotations of half-integer spinors; time reversal is not included automatically.

entries.title: Antiunitary operators and complex conjugation
entries.definition: An antiunitary action is a matrix followed by complex conjugation; multiplication may require conjugating the second matrix.

variables.meaning: Complex conjugation in the chosen basis
Matrix part of an antiunitary operation

entries.conventions: (AK)(BK)=AB*, rather than the ordinary matrix product AB.
entries.conditions: Used for magnetic corepresentations, time reversal, and spin space groups; the basis must be specified.

entries.title: Time reversal and the Kramers condition
entries.definition: An antiunitary symmetry guarantees Kramers pairing if it preserves the selected k and squares to −1.

variables.meaning: Depends on the spin and any accompanying translation

entries.conventions: The time-reversal square is commonly +1 without spin and −1 for spin 1/2; combined magnetic translations also contribute a Bloch phase.
entries.conditions: It is not enough to see the 2D representation or S²=−1 formula, one must check that the states are brought back to the same k.

entries.title: Periodic Bloch gauge
entries.definition: uses lattice translation to construct the orbital base marked by wavevector . The sign of the exponent and whether the orbital center is included must be fixed.

variables.meaning: Orbital center within the primitive cell

entries.conventions: site induction module uses Σ_T exp(+2πik·T)|T+rₐ⟩; the translation eigenvalue is exp(−2πik·L).
entries.conditions: Other modules may use different gauges. Transform to a common gauge before comparing matrices.

entries.title: k: wavevector in reciprocal fractional coordinates
entries.definition: Expresses a wavevector in the reciprocal basis; components differing by integers describe the same crystal momentum.

variables.meaning: Fractional components in the reciprocal basis
Phase angle in the Bloch exponential

entries.conventions: This site's space group , site induction, and Phonopy imports usually use 2π explicitly; the module annotation shall prevail.
entries.conditions: Do not combine these coordinates algebraically with a model wavevector expressed in radians without converting conventions.

entries.title: k: model wavevector in radians
entries.definition: Some tight-binding teaching models absorb the lattice constant into k, allowing Brillouin zone to be written −π to π.

variables.unit: rad or a⁻¹, depending on the module

variables.meaning: Lattice constant absorbed into the coordinates

entries.conventions: If H(k) uses sin k and cos k, this convention is often used; it cannot be multiplied by 2π additionally.
entries.conditions: This entry describes that convention only; use the actual input definitions and plot axes to determine the coordinates in use.

entries.title: Γ: Brillouin-zone center
entries.definition: The Γ point has zero crystal momentum, k=(0,0,0).

variables.unit: Coordinate units depend on the module

entries.conventions: Γ as k-point differs from the subscripted electrode broadening Γ_L, Γ_R, and also from the Γ label of some irreducible representation .
entries.conditions: The symbol Γ alone does not determine which meaning is intended.

entries.title: Γ: lead-coupling broadening matrix
entries.definition: The anti-Hermitian part of the lead self-energy determines the coupling broadening that enters coherent-transport transmission.

variables.unit: The same energy unit as the Hamiltonian, usually eV on this site

entries.conventions: With the retarded-self-energy convention, Γ_α is normally positive semidefinite. This Γ is not the Γ point.
entries.conditions: An elastic, noninteracting two-terminal model is assumed. The numerical broadening parameter η is a separate quantity.

entries.title: U: unitary transformation or representation matrix
entries.definition: Unitary matrices preserve state inner products and can describe changes of basis, time evolution, or the linear part of symmetry operations.

variables.meaning: Matrix acting in the specified state space

entries.conventions: U†U=I; here U does not denote an electronic on-site repulsion energy.
entries.conditions: Check the input and output bases of U. An antiunitary action also requires complex conjugation K.

entries.title: U: electronic on-site interaction energy
entries.definition: The energy cost when electrons with different spins occupy the same local orbit at the same time; the multi-orbital model also needs to distinguish between U′ and Hund coupling.

variables.meaning: On-site repulsion within the same orbital
variables.unit: Usually eV on this site; some models use t as the energy unit

entries.conventions: single-band Hubbard entry is UΣ_i n_i↑n_i↓; it is not unitary matrix .
entries.conditions: Exact diagonalization of a small cluster does not by itself give an infinite-lattice phase diagram or fit the parameters of a real material.

entries.title: U: independent spin action in a spin group
entries.definition: Spin groups pair real-space operations with independent spin rotations; their spatial and spin actions need not coincide.

variables.meaning: Rotation of spin directions or its spinor matrix
variables.unit: Dimensionless; the representation space depends on the module

entries.conventions: distinguishes between classical three-component spin rotation and two-component SU(2) spinor; locking constraints need to be checked when strong SOC.
entries.conditions: Not every independent spin rotation preserves the chosen magnetic order, nor does it automatically apply to systems with SOC.

entries.title: J: exchange-coupling constant
entries.definition: Coefficients in the spin Hamiltonian that control the relative arrangement of adjacent spins.

variables.unit: Energy; commonly meV on this site

variables.meaning: Spin operator or classical spin direction
variables.unit: Whether ℏ is included depends on the module

entries.conventions: Positive J has opposite ferromagnetic/antiferromagnetic meanings in H=+J S_i·S_j and H=−J S_i·S_j; inspect the actual formula.
entries.conditions: Linear spin-wave theory also assumes small fluctuations about the specified stable magnetic order.

entries.title: J: Hund coupling
entries.definition: In multiorbital interactions, Hund coupling controls spin preferences between different orbitals and is related to exchange, spin-flip, and pair-hopping terms.

variables.unit: Energy, commonly eV on this site

entries.conventions: Rotationally invariant Kanamori parameters commonly obey U′=U−2J; retain the terms actually implemented by the module.
entries.conditions: A single Hund parameter cannot be equated to a full Slater integral or a full atomic multiplet spectrum.

entries.title: J: total angular momentum and its quantum number
entries.definition: The total-angular-momentum operator or its quantum number; distinguish the meaning from capitalization and context.
entries.conventions: Many demonstrations set ℏ=1; the output is reduced angular momentum in units of ℏ.
entries.conditions: J need not remain an exact good quantum number in a crystal field with spin–orbit coupling.

entries.title: SU(2) and spinors
entries.definition: The group of 2×2 unitary matrices with determinant 1; it describes spin-1/2 spinors and Bloch-sphere rotations.
entries.conventions: spin 1/2 rotation is often taken as U=exp(−iθ n·σ/2), and 2π rotation changes the sign of the state.
entries.conditions: The Bloch sphere represents rays of pure two-level states, not the real-space position of an object.

entries.title: Dynkin labels of SU(3)
entries.definition: Labels an SU(3) highest-weight representation by two nonnegative integers (p,q).
entries.conventions: Fundamental 3=(1,0), conjugate 3̅=(0,1), and adjoint 8=(1,1).
entries.conditions: SU(3) representations and three-dimensional crystallographic space-group representations use different labeling systems.

entries.title: Clebsch–Gordan change-of-basis coefficients
entries.definition: Elements of a unitary change-of-basis matrix connecting the tensor-product basis to the coupled irreducible-component basis.

variables.meaning: Change-of-basis coefficient for the chosen phases and basis ordering

entries.conventions: The overall phase of each irreducible block and the multiplicity space basis can be changed; the coefficients must be agreed before comparison.
entries.conditions: SU(3) may exist outer multiplicity ; only reporting representation dimension cannot uniquely determine Clebsch–Gordan coefficients .

entries.title: Racah / 6j recoupling
entries.definition: Relates the two bracketings of successive couplings in a triple tensor product.
entries.conventions: matrix depends on the CG phase and channel basis; the scalar 6j of SU(2) cannot be mixed with the SU(3) containing outer multiplicity case.
entries.conditions: Compare the same total output representation and the complete channel space.

entries.title: 9j coefficients and four-body recoupling
entries.definition: The overlap or change of basis between two pairwise-coupling schemes in a fourfold tensor product.

variables.meaning: Change-of-basis matrix for fixed output representation and multiplicity channels

entries.conventions: An individual coefficient can change sign under a different convention. Check the full orthogonality or unitarity relations instead.
entries.conditions: Higher-dimensional exact results remain subject to resource limits; SU(3) channels can carry outer multiplicity.

entries.title: Berry phase
entries.definition: Geometric phase accumulated by a state under parallel transport around a closed path in parameter space.

variables.meaning: Geometric phase around a closed loop

entries.conventions: The phase of the discrete overlap product requires a fixed loop direction; the local phase of a single state is not an observable.
entries.conditions: A degenerate occupied subspace requires subspace overlaps and a non-Abelian construction.

entries.title: Berry curvature
entries.definition: The local curvature of the geometric phase in parameter space can participate in anomalous velocities and intrinsic Hall responses.

variables.meaning: Curvature component with respect to the chosen k coordinates
variables.unit: Length² when k has units of length⁻¹; dimensionless for reduced k

entries.conventions: Signs depend on the Berry-connection and loop-orientation conventions; use the Chern and Hall formulas from the same module.
entries.conditions: Use single-band expressions carefully near band crossings, and check the gap and mesh convergence in numerical integration.

entries.title: Quantum metric
entries.definition: The real part of the quantum geometric tensor, measuring the infinitesimal distance between neighboring quantum-state rays.

variables.unit: Determined by the units of the chosen parameter coordinates
Also depends on the parameter coordinates

entries.conventions: Gauge invariant, although the component units and numerical values change with the parameter coordinates.
entries.conditions: requires isolated states or explicit multi-band projected subspaces and cannot be compared directly with arbitrary degenerate eigenvectors.

entries.title: Chern number
entries.definition: An integral invariant of the occupied-subspace Berry curvature over a closed two-dimensional Brillouin zone.
entries.conventions: is commonly used C=(1/2π)∫Ω d²k; it must be consistent with the curvature sign and orientation.
entries.conditions: Must have separate occupied subspaces and check mesh convergence; metallic part occupation integrals are usually not integer Chern numbers.

entries.title: Wilson loops and subspace parallel transport
entries.definition: Multiply occupied-subspace overlap matrices along a closed path to obtain a gauge-covariant matrix with gauge-invariant eigenphases.
entries.conventions: requires consistent number of occupied bands and period endpoint handling; labels for individual phase branches are interchangeable.
entries.conditions: An arbitrary finite-mesh output does not automatically establish a complete Z₂ or topological classification.

entries.title: Tight-binding Bloch Hamiltonian
entries.definition: Energy matrix obtained by Fourier transforming hopping between orbitals in different cells.

variables.unit: Energy, commonly eV on this site
Integer lattice coordinates or reduced lengths

entries.conventions: Follow the module's conventions for the sign of the exponential, factors of 2π, and orbital centers; H(k) must be Hermitian.
entries.conditions: Teaching model parameters are not the default DFT fitting results, nor do they automatically include interactions.

entries.title: Fermi–Dirac occupation
entries.definition: Equilibrium mean occupation of a fermionic level at a specified temperature and chemical potential.

variables.unit: The same energy unit as E
The same energy unit as E

entries.conventions: f=1/[exp((E−μ)/(k_B T))+1]; The zero temperature limit needs to be clearly processed at the Fermi surface.
entries.conditions: Thermal occupations do not automatically impose a fixed particle number. At fixed N, μ must be determined separately.

entries.title: Seebeck coefficient
entries.definition: Linear-response coefficient relating the temperature gradient to the open-circuit electric field.

variables.unit: V/K, usually displayed as μV/K on this site
s; some ratios cancel τ in the constant-relaxation-time approximation

entries.conventions: sign depends on the electric field, temperature gradient and charge definition, using the j=0 convention given by the module.
entries.conditions: The constant relaxation time and band model limit the accuracy; σ/τ is not the actual σ.

entries.title: intrinsic anomalous Hall response
entries.definition: Occupancy weighted Berry Curvature integration gives the intrinsic transverse electrical response.

variables.meaning: Two-dimensional sheet conductance or three-dimensional conductivity
variables.unit: 2D is usually e²/h; 3D is usually S/m, depending on the module

entries.conventions: 2D model cannot be directly written as a 3D bulk conductivity.
entries.conditions: This QWZ model includes neither extrinsic scattering mechanisms nor full material transport.

entries.title: Transverse thermoelectric α versus the Nernst effect
entries.definition: α_xy describes the transverse thermoelectric current response. Finding an open-circuit Nernst voltage additionally requires the full electrical conductivity tensor.

variables.unit: The two-dimensional and three-dimensional units are different and are displayed according to the module.

entries.conventions: The α_xy curve cannot be directly marked as Nernst voltage; the tensor inversion and sign need to be checked.
entries.conditions: The current teaching module primarily provides intrinsic contributions of noninteracting models.

entries.title: Retarded Green function
entries.definition: The retarded resolvent commonly used in spectra and transport; a positive imaginary part selects the corresponding causal boundary condition.

variables.unit: Energy, commonly eV on this site

entries.conventions: η>0; The physical meanings of electrode coupling broadening Γ and η are different.
entries.conditions: Finite eta will smooth the discrete spectrum and affect the peak height, so convergence needs to be checked.

entries.title: Landauer transmission and conductance
entries.definition: coherent two-terminal model, the transmission probability determines the linear response conductance.

variables.unit: e²/h times the degeneracy, or S

entries.conventions: The multiple of the independent spin channel must be explicitly included and cannot be multiplied by 2 unconditionally.
entries.conditions: Elastic, coherent, non-interactive assumptions; transmission probability is not equal to finite bias current.

entries.title: Andreev Reflection
entries.definition: The process in which electrons are incident on the normal metal-superconducting interface and then converted into hole reflection, and the paired condensate absorbs the charge.
entries.conventions: BdG electron/hole basis and flux normalization must be consistent; conductance also includes ordinary reflection contributions.
entries.conditions: tutorial model does not include self-consistent order parameter , inelastic scattering, or any real contacts.

entries.title: Crystal-field splitting and orbitals
entries.definition: The local environment causes the orbital energy levels of the same atomic shell to split, and the coefficient definitions and coordinate axes must be fixed.

variables.meaning: Energy separation between two groups of levels in the selected geometry

entries.conventions: The positive Δ energy level order of octahedron and tetrahedron is different; some definitions use 10Dq.
entries.conditions: single-electron energy level model cannot directly predict multi-electron high and low spin or complete experimental spectra.

entries.title: Kanamori Multi-orbital interaction
entries.definition: Density repulsion, Hund exchange, spin flips, and pair hopping describe a selected multiorbital subspace.

variables.unit: has the same unit as U

entries.conventions: Check both the module's parameter relations and the terms it actually retains; U≥3J is a constraint on some teaching inputs.
entries.conditions: This is not a complete atomic Slater-integral model; material parameters also depend on screening and the basis.

entries.title: Optical dipole moment and polarization selection rule
entries.definition: Transition intensity is related to the squared modulus of the dipole matrix element projected along the polarization direction.

variables.unit: charge × length; reduced model unit according to module

entries.conventions: Intensities are often relative; distinguish amplitudes, squared moduli, and averages over degenerate states.
entries.conditions: The electric-dipole approximation does not automatically include magnetic-dipole or phonon-assisted processes, or actual linewidths.

entries.title: Effective Spin and Magnetic Resonance
entries.definition: describes Zeeman and zero-field splitting and transitions in terms of finite-dimensional effective spin Hamiltonians.

variables.unit: According to the module, it is energy or frequency, and the conversion must be consistent.

entries.conventions: spin matrix is often used as ℏ=1; frequency energy is converted to E=hν.
entries.conditions: The effective spin model does not amount to an ab initio solution for the entire electron shell.

entries.title: phonon dynamical matrix
entries.definition: The Fourier-transformed, mass-weighted force-constant matrix; its eigenvalues give squared angular frequencies.

variables.unit: rad/s; software frequency can also use conventions such as THz

entries.conventions: If the frequency ν is displayed, ω=2πν; negative eigenvalues usually represent unstable modes with imaginary frequency symbols.
entries.conditions: Arbitrary positive and negative frequency data do not automatically satisfy acoustic sum rules or force constant convergence.

entries.title: Mass-weighted phonon eigenvector
entries.definition: Phonon eigenvector normalization and mass factors determine physical atomic displacements and scattering amplitudes.
entries.conventions: Phonopy related input is often u_j∝e_j/√M_j; the eigenvector components cannot be directly regarded as equal-amplitude atomic displacements.
entries.conditions: Degenerate modes admit changes of basis; use the entire degenerate subspace when comparing physical observables.

entries.title: Density of states and integral weight
entries.definition: describes the number of modes in terms of frequency or energy distribution, and the normalization depends on each cell, each atom and the input weight.

variables.unit: Per frequency or per energy; in horizontal axis units

entries.conventions: When changing from frequency to energy axis, the corresponding Jacobian is required; you cannot just change the graph axis text.
entries.conditions: Thermodynamic integration requires coverage of the complete grid or correct DOS normalization, and energy band paths are not sufficient to replace full-area sampling.

entries.title: Vibration free energy and heat capacity
entries.definition: Harmonic-oscillator frequencies and Bose occupations determine vibrational free energy, entropy, and constant-volume heat capacity.

variables.unit: units per cell or mole according to module

entries.conventions: is ½ℏω; the frequency ν and angular frequency ω need to be converted correctly.
entries.conditions: Imaginary frequencies cannot be directly inserted into stable harmonic-oscillator thermodynamic formulas.

entries.title: Quasiharmonic approximation and thermal expansion
entries.definition: Determine temperature-dependent equilibrium volume using static energies at several volumes and volume-dependent phonon free energies.

variables.unit: According to the structural unit, it is usually Å³/ cell

entries.conventions: Each volume still uses harmonic oscillators; temperature effects enter through the volume dependence of frequencies.
entries.conditions: Single volume data cannot be called a complete QHA; phase instability and strong anharmonic regions require additional methods.

entries.title: Neumann principle and physical-property tensor
entries.definition: material physical-property tensor must remain unchanged under its allowed symmetry, and the independent components can be found accordingly.

variables.unit: is determined by physical properties such as dielectric/elasticity/piezoelectricity

entries.conventions: Polar/axial character and time-reversal parity determine extra signs; equal tensor rank does not imply equal transformation laws.
entries.conditions: symmetry only constrains the allowed components and does not give the actual size of the material components.

entries.title: Second-harmonic generation and susceptibility
entries.definition: The second-order optical susceptibility couples two incident-field components into a polarization at twice the frequency.

variables.unit: SI is usually m/V, and the teaching diagram can be normalized to relative units.

entries.conventions: The amplitude is first projected to the exit polarization and then the modulus is squared; the complete tensor must be transformed when rotating the crystal.
entries.conditions: Bulk electric-dipole SHG is forbidden in inversion-symmetric crystals. Surface, magnetic-dipole, and other mechanisms are outside this simple criterion.

entries.title: Landau order parameter Free Energy
entries.definition: Expand the free energy according to order parameter and the terms allowed by the symmetry, and then analyze the stationary point, stability and phase transition.

variables.meaning: order parameter ; sometimes polarization, sometimes dimensionless amplitude

variables.unit: is determined by P and free energy units

entries.conventions: Only stationary points with positive second-order derivatives are local minima; free energy needs to be compared to determine global stability.
entries.conditions: coefficients are teaching parameters and do not automatically correspond to the temperature function of a specific real material.

entries.title: Diffraction structure factor and extinction
entries.definition: Add complex amplitudes from the primitive-cell scatterers, then take the squared modulus for intensity. Site phases can cause extinction.

variables.meaning: Scattering factor or coherent scattering length

entries.conventions: Distinguish lattice systematic absences, basis-interference zeros, and merely small structure factors. The wavelength affects which reflections are accessible.
entries.conditions: A teaching stick spectrum is not a complete experimental pattern with multiple scattering, instrumental resolution, and actual atomic form factors.

entries.title: supercell band unfolding Weight
entries.definition: Project supercell eigenstates onto primitive-translation eigensectors to recover primitive-cell momentum-resolved spectral weights.

variables.meaning: weight of selected primitive cell k sectors

entries.conventions: Unfolding weights depend on the primitive/supercell mapping and orbital correspondence; a spectral weight is not an additional eigenband.
entries.conditions: For disorder, defects, or magnetic supercells, retain a consistent orbital gauge and verify weight sum rules.

entries.title: Site-induced Bloch band representation
entries.definition: Construct a periodic orbital basis from a real-space seed, its site stabilizer, and the complete orbit of sites; this determines the group action in each k fiber.

variables.meaning: Site-orbit multiplicity within the primitive cell
Local orbital dimension of each site

entries.conventions: fiber dimension is m × d; this is different from inducing the entire k-star from momentum little group .
entries.conditions: selects SG2/4/19/221, no spin s/p; does not automatically determine the elementary properties or material topology of EBR.

entries.title: Site orbits and stabilizers
entries.definition: The site stabilizer contains operations that genuinely fix the seed; the orbit–stabilizer relation controls the induced dimension.

variables.unit: Finite point group, order is integer

variables.meaning: Number of orbit sites within the primitive cell

entries.conventions: If Rr₀+t=r₀+L, use the operation with translation part t−L to fix r₀ exactly.
entries.conditions: must be counted under the action of the same primitive cell and the same space group , and cannot be mixed with k star arm numbers.

entries.title: Screw square and Bloch phase
entries.definition: Applying a spinless 2₁ screw twice gives a full lattice translation; its axial eigenvalues acquire a k-dependent phase.

variables.meaning: reciprocal lattice component along screw axis

entries.conventions: U_S²=exp(−2πikz)I, so λ±=±exp(−iπkz), the boundary kz=1/2 is given to ±i.
entries.conditions: The operation must actually preserve the selected k; double-valued spin representations contribute an extra spinor sign.

entries.title: dynamic structure factor S(Q,ω)
entries.definition: Frequency- and momentum-resolved density or spin correlation spectra determine the measurable intensity under the chosen scattering approximation.

variables.unit: Å⁻¹ or reciprocal lattice unit, according to module

variables.meaning: angular frequency; energy transfer can also be used ℏω
variables.unit: according to the drawing axis unit

entries.conventions: Nuclear phonon scattering and magnetic spin scattering use different operators, mass factors, and polarization projections.
entries.conditions: The same energy position does not mean the same peak intensity; the form factor, temperature, broadening and normalization need to be checked.

entries.title: Transverse polarization projection of magnetic scattering
entries.definition: Magnetic scattering only detects the fluctuation component of the magnetic moment perpendicular to the direction of momentum transfer.
entries.conventions: At Q=0 the direction is undefined; use the declared limit or disable that point.
entries.conditions: Without actual magnetic form factors and all instrumental factors, call the output a relative model intensity.

entries.title: Bose Factors and Detailed Balance
entries.definition: In thermal equilibrium, occupations and detailed balance relate scattering weights on the energy-loss and energy-gain sides.
entries.conventions: First fix positive/negative energy-transfer conventions. Creating an excitation has weight n_B+1; annihilating one has weight n_B.
entries.conditions: Zero temperature and zero frequency limits require special processing and should not be divided by zero directly.

entries.title: domain wall with continuous order parameter profile
entries.definition: Spatially non-uniform solution connecting two different order parameter minima, wall width and energy depend on local potential and gradient cost.

variables.unit: According to the model, it is often the reduced dimensionless amplitude
According to the module, usually the reduced length

entries.conventions: Simple symmetrical φ⁴ models can have tanh-shaped walls; this does not mean that all real ferroelectric or magnetic domain wall are of the same form.
entries.conditions: Actual charged domain walls, elastic constraints, and multicomponent rotations require additional electric-field and coupling terms.

entries.title: Ginzburg gradient energy and wall width
entries.definition: The energy cost of spatially nonuniform order parameters; together with the local potential it determines the wall thickness.

variables.unit: is determined by free energy, order parameter and length unit

entries.conventions: is commonly used as f_grad=κ(∂P/∂x)²/2; omitting 1/2 will change the coefficient and analytical wall width definition.
entries.conditions: only compares wall width values ​​using the same functional normalization and boundary conditions.

entries.title: Hubbard small clusters and many-body substrates
entries.definition: Retain hopping and local interactions in the Fock space of a specified particle number on a finite set of lattice sites.

variables.unit: eV or selected energy unit according to module

entries.conventions: The sign generated by fermion exchange must be retained; the many-body basis cannot be directly used as a single-particle orbital basis.
entries.conditions: The energy gaps, spectral peaks and correlations of finite clusters are not equal to the complete Mott phase transition at the thermodynamic limit.

entries.title: Double occupancy and local correlation
entries.definition: Double occupation measures the probability of having up and down spin electrons in the same orbit at the same time, and is a diagnostic quantity of the local repulsion effect.

variables.unit: Dimensionless; its range depends on the number of lattice sites

entries.conventions: It is necessary to specify each point or the total quantity; the non-interaction finite temperature value can also be non-zero.
entries.conditions: The double occupation decrease itself cannot prove the existence of Mott insulating phase in the infinite system.

entries.title: Many-body spectral function and Lehmann weight
entries.definition: Electron addition/removal of matrix elements and energy difference constitute a spectral function that can display discrete peaks generated by interactions.

variables.meaning: Here energy transfer is commonly used as the horizontal axis
variables.unit: is eV or reduced energy according to module

entries.conventions: Spectral weight summation rules depend on the operator, whether to sum spins/sites, and normalization.
entries.conditions: The discrete peak plus broadening of small clusters is not an infinite lattice continuous spectrum, and the peak width should not be interpreted as lifetime.

entries.title: Point operation name, axis label and rotation direction
entries.definition: Operation names retain upstream BC labels. A subscript may combine a rotation order and an axis index; do not interpret it as a space-group screw subscript.

variables.meaning: Twofold-rotation operation label; the rotation matrix defines the actual action
Rotation direction or axis label in upstream convention, does not necessarily mean time reversal

entries.conventions: For example, 31 in C31+ is one complete operation subscript, not automatically a 3₁ screw. Distinguish magnetic-group primes from BC axis primes using context.
entries.conditions: To determine the actual operation and axis direction, please check the corresponding R and t matrices. Do not just guess based on the name.

entries.title: Schönflies point group Symbol
entries.definition: A set of symbols labeled point group with primary rotation axes, mirrors, and other generating operations.

variables.meaning: A point group with a principal threefold axis and vertical mirrors
Full cubic point group including inversion

entries.conventions: The 3v in C3v is one complete subscript. HM lattice notation C2 and Schönflies C₂ use different syntax.
entries.conditions: The three-dimensional point group tag is not a direct replacement for the full definition of space group , the magnetic group, or double group .

entries.title: Angular frequency ω, frequency ν and energy transfer
entries.definition: frequency ν counts cycles per second, angular frequency ω counts radians per second, and quantum energy corresponds to hν=ℏω.

variables.unit: Hz; the module may also use THz or GHz
rad/s; if the horizontal axis is changed to ℏω, it is energy

entries.conventions: The THz frequency cannot be directly regarded as the angular frequency and then multiplied by ℏ; first check the conversion of the module's horizontal axis and h/ℏ.
entries.conditions: The same ω letters may also represent Berry curvature components in quantum geometry, which must be combined with the current module and subscripts.

entries.title: Multibody addition, removal spectra and Lehmann expansion
entries.definition: Decompose electron-addition/removal spectra into transitions from many-body initial states to final states with neighboring particle numbers. Energy differences fix peak positions; actual matrix elements determine visibility.

variables.meaning: Addition/removal spectral density for a specified orbital and spin
Energy reference chemical potential of adjacent particle number spectrum

entries.conventions: Added using c†, removed using c; the energy reference of the frequency axis, the selected particle number sector and the degenerate average must be noted. The horizontal axis of the spectrum here uses energy.
entries.conditions: The discrete transitions of finite clusters are not equivalent to the macroscopic material continuum; a single energy level difference does not guarantee non-zero transition intensity.

entries.title: Transition spectrum weight and Fermi sum rule
entries.definition: A transition spectral weight is the squared modulus of its transition matrix element, averaged with the stated initial-state probabilities. For a local single-spin electron spectrum, the sum of addition and removal weights is fixed by the fermionic anticommutation relation.

variables.meaning: Weight from initial state i to final state f
Integrated weight of the complete addition spectrum
Integrated weight of the complete removal spectrum

entries.conventions: W_remove=⟨n_{iσ}⟩, W_add=1−⟨n_{iσ}⟩ under normalized local operator. The numerical integration of the broadened finite energy window may miss the tail; the unbroadened weight sum should be checked separately.
entries.conditions: Summing over orbitals or spins, or changing transition operators, changes normalization. This local sum rule cannot be applied mechanically to arbitrary responses.

entries.title: spectral line broadening η and Lorentz half-maximum half-width
entries.definition: Energy broadening used to draw discrete spectral peaks as finite-width Lorentzian curves. This many-body spectra experiment uses it as a display and analytic-continuation parameter.

variables.meaning: Lorentz curve half height half width
Spectral coordinates relative to the specified energy reference

entries.conventions: Lorentz shape is (η/π)/[(E−E_f)²+η²], full width at half maximum is 2η. The value η is not the decoherence rate γ of the density matrix module, nor does it automatically correspond to the measured life.
entries.conditions: Check half-width at half-maximum, full width at half-maximum, and energy/frequency units before comparing linewidths. Finite windows omit some Lorentzian tails.

entries.title: Onsite repulsion U in the many-body spectral model
entries.definition: The interaction energy for opposite-spin electrons doubly occupying one site in the Hubbard spectral experiment; it changes neighboring particle-number sectors and transition weights.
entries.conventions: contains UΣ_i n_{i↑}n_{i↓} in the Hamiltonian; U here is a real energy parameter, not unitary matrix in the crystal representation.
entries.conditions: is only for the current finite single orbital cluster, and the macroscopic Mott phase transition cannot be asserted by the U size alone.

entries.title: Holstein local electron–phonon coupling g
entries.definition: In this site's two-site Holstein model, local electron occupation couples to dimensionless oscillator displacement, modulating site energies rather than directly changing hopping.

variables.meaning: Electronic occupation of the i-th site

entries.conventions: H_ep=gΣ_i n_i X_i. The Latin letter g here is neither the Brillouin zone center marked by the Greek letter Γ, nor the dimensionless g factor of magnetic resonance.
entries.conditions: model fixes one electron and two independent local oscillators; there is no automatic fitting of the electron- phonon matrix element from the Phonopy file.

entries.title: Vibrational cloud conditioned on electron location
entries.definition: First limit the electron to be located at site i, and then observe the average dimensionless displacement of oscillator j. Joint correlations reveal hidden vibrational clouds in uniform electron densities.

variables.meaning: b_j+b_j†, not the real atomic displacement expressed as Å
Joint expectation of electron occupation and oscillator displacement

entries.conventions: conditional displacement is equal to ⟨n_i X_j⟩/⟨n_i⟩; it is not defined when the denominator is close to zero. Uniform electron density does not imply zero joint correlation.
entries.conditions: Conditional displacement alone is not evidence of spontaneous symmetry breaking. This two-site model does not determine actual polaron radii or self-trapping critical points.

entries.title: phonon Truncation and top-level probability
entries.definition: limits the infinite number state space of each oscillator from 0 to N_max to obtain a diagonalizable finite matrix; the impact of the deleted space needs to be additionally checked.

variables.meaning: Maximum allowed number of phonon per local oscillator
The probability that the i-th oscillator is located in the highest allowed layer
The absolute value of the energy difference between adjacent truncated ground states

entries.conventions: The model dimension is 2(N_max+1)². Adjacent-cutoff checks examine energies, local observables, and highest-level probabilities. Eigenstate residuals test the finite matrix, not convergence with the cutoff.
entries.conditions: The current parameter inspection does not guarantee that the entire coupling scan converges; the adjacent truncation difference is not a strict upper bound of the global error.

entries.title: density matrix and Bloch vectors
entries.definition: density matrix Unified represents pure states and statistical mixtures; in a specified basis, the diagonal elements measure probability and the off-diagonal elements record coherence.

variables.meaning: Hermitian , positive semi-definite state operator with trace 1
Coherence matrix element with fixed z basis
Bloch vector, the components are the expected values of the Pauli matrix

entries.conventions: single spin ρ=(I+r·σ)/2; base ↑, ↓, double spin sorted by ↑↑, ↑↓, ↓↑, ↓↓. change of basis changes the matrix elements without changing the purity.
entries.conditions: The module needs to be checked before interpreting ρ as mass density or charge density; this entry only refers to quantum states.

entries.title: overall purity and reduced purity
entries.definition: density matrix The trace of the square describes the degree of mixing of the state. The purity of the finite-dimensional normalized pure state is 1, and the purity of the maximum mixed state is the reciprocal of the dimension.
entries.conventions: 1/d≤P≤1. The reduction in the reduced purity of the overall pure state is related to the subsystem entanglement ; when the overall state is already in a mixed state, classical mixing can also reduce the reduced purity.
entries.conditions: purity is not a general mixed entanglement measure; low purity cannot be directly read as stronger entanglement .

entries.title: partial trace , reduced state and local entropy
entries.definition: Take partial trace for the unobserved subsystem B to obtain the reduced state of A; the local entropy measures the mixing of A, but generally includes both classical statistics and quantum entanglement effects.

variables.meaning: Tr_Bρ, the reduced density matrix of subsystem A
Trace over the basis index of B

entries.conventions: Only when the overall pure state is present, S(ρ_A) is the entanglement entropy of the bisection. Both singlet and antiparallel classical mixtures can have ρ_A=I/2 and local entropy 1 bit.
entries.conditions: local measurements alone cannot reconstruct all global correlations; the overall state and appropriate criteria are also required when comparing entanglement .

entries.title: Partially transposed negativity: double spin mixed state entanglement
entries.definition: After partially transposing the B subsystem, the absolute values of the negative eigenvalues are added to obtain the entanglement quantity that can be used for this double-spin mixed state.

variables.meaning: Transpose matrix index of B in fixed product basis
Trace norm of partially transposed matrix

entries.conventions: N(ρ)=(||ρ^{T_B}||_1−1)/2; singlet is 1/2, antiparallel classical mixing is 0. It is different from local entropy.
entries.conditions: This experiment is a 2×2 system, and zero negativity corresponds to a separable state; do not directly extrapolate this completeness to all high-dimensional mixed states.

entries.title: Lindblad relaxation and pure-dephasing rates
entries.definition: uses fixed Markov channels to describe population relaxation and coherent decay; here γ is the rate and cannot be directly mixed with the broadening eta in energy in the spectral function.

variables.meaning: Pure-dephasing rate produced by the σ_z channel
γ_1/2+γ_φ, transverse envelope rate of free single spin without drive

entries.conventions: C_1=√γ_1 |↓⟩⟨↑|, C_φ=√(γ_φ/2)σ_z. The subscript and unit of γ must be retained; the capital Γ also often indicates Brillouin zone center or electrode broadening.
entries.conditions: Driven or exchange-coupled curves need not be single exponentials. Fixed local channels do not automatically satisfy thermal detailed balance for an interacting Hamiltonian.

entries.title: Spin drive angular frequency Ω
entries.definition: The transverse coefficient of the single spin Hamiltonian divided by ℏ controls the resonant Rabi rotation. It uses the same letters as Berry curvature in quantum geometry but has different meanings and units.
entries.conventions: On resonance, without dissipation and starting from ↑, P_↑(t)=cos²(Ωt/2). Do not treat rad/ns as cycles/ns.
entries.conditions: A constant effective-drive model, without full experimental pulses, rotating-wave-approximation errors, or actual instrumental noise.

entries.title: Exchange angular frequency in double spin evolution J
entries.definition: In the density matrix experiment, J is the coefficient of S_A·S_B in H/ℏ, setting the phase evolution scale between the singlet and triplet states.

variables.meaning: The exchange energy is divided by ℏ

entries.conventions: Positive J gives antiferromagnetic exchange. The singlet/triplet eigenvalues of H/ℏ are −3J/4 and J/4. This input is not an energy in eV as in the Hubbard interface; conversion requires ℏ.
entries.conditions: The dual-spin model ignores charge fluctuations in the Hubbard model; only after accounting for low-energy conditions and unit conversion can the exchange scale of the two modules be compared.

entries.title: Symmetry constraints and Pauli band splitting
entries.definition: Write the two-dimensional 2×2 Hamiltonian as the unit matrix term and three Pauli terms, apply the generator identity to all momentum, and find the allowed real coefficient space.

variables.meaning: Symmetry operation matrix of real spin doublets
Common energy shift of both bands

entries.conventions: Unitary space operations satisfy H(Rk)=UH(k)U†; antiunitary operation also contains complex conjugation . Energy E_±=d_0±|d|. The workshop uses a second-order expansion around Γ and a Euclidean orthogonal projection with specified monomial coefficients.
entries.conditions: Projected coefficients are not material fits. Disabling a generator no longer preserves the original group, and a local gap alone does not give a full-Brillouin-zone topological number.

entries.title: polar vector and axial vector under the mirror
entries.definition: Momentum is a polar vector transforming by R; physical spin is axial and transforms by det(R)R. Their mirror actions differ.

variables.meaning: Transformation matrix of spin axial vector
Pauli matrix vector of real spin doublet state

entries.conventions: The xz mirror makes (k_x,k_y)→(k_x,−k_y), makes (σ_x,σ_y,σ_z)→(−σ_x,σ_y,−σ_z). The inversion causes the momentum to change sign but the true spin to remain unchanged.
entries.conditions: is only applicable to the same-parity real spin doublet state declared by the workshop; any orbital pseudo-spin needs to use its actual small representation, and the axial vector rule cannot be copied.

entries.title: order parameter vector
entries.definition: To describe the order direction and magnitude using vectors in representation space, one must first declare how the group acts.
entries.conventions: C₄ᵥ uses xy two-dimensional polar vector ; O_h uses xyz three-dimensional polar vector , and the inversion is −I.
entries.conditions: is not equivalent to the real atomic mode or absolute polarization; it has a different meaning from the spectral line broadening eta.

entries.title: stabilizer subgroup and parent group orbit
entries.definition: Operations preserving the specified order parameter form its stabilizer subgroup; the parent-group orbit contains every symmetry-related state.
entries.conventions: |Gη|=|G|/|H_η|; Different operations can give the same orbit status.
entries.conditions: When there is an explicit external field, the states in the parent group orbit are no longer necessarily isoenergetic; a given direction is not equal to the equilibrium phase.

entries.title: Reynolds Group mean and invariant
entries.definition: averages the polynomials after the finite group action and projects them into the invariant polynomial space.
entries.conventions: P_G f=(1/|G|)Σ_g f(D(g)η) is a linear idempotent projection; zero images and repeated images cannot be regarded as independent bases.
entries.conditions: This experiment uses signed-permutation representations and outputs orbit sums normalized to minimal integer coefficients. It does not determine free-energy coefficients automatically.

entries.title: Passive coordinate transformation
entries.definition: Change axes that describe the same physical state and transform all vectors, tensors, and operations simultaneously.

variables.meaning: column vector of the new coordinate axis in the old coordinate

entries.conventions: v′=Qᵀv, R′=QᵀRQ; scalar function F′(v′)=F(Qv′).
entries.conditions: Different from just rotating the physical vector and keeping the laboratory energy expression unchanged; the quantum basis transformation must use the corresponding unitary U.

entries.title: Directed-bond exchange tensor
entries.definition: couples the real spins of the two sites through a general real 3×3 matrix.

variables.meaning: Exchange tensor for the directed bond i→j
i spin, quantum calculation is σ/2

entries.conventions: H_ij=S_iᵀJ_ijS_j; J_ji=J_ijᵀ when exchanging endpoints. The constraint must distinguish whether the operation swaps both ends.
entries.conditions: A general bulk-property tensor cannot replace bond constraints. Symmetry fixes allowed forms, not parameter magnitudes.

entries.title: Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya vector
entries.definition: The axial vector associated with the exchange tensor's antisymmetric part, defining the D·(S_i×S_j) term.

variables.meaning: DMI vector dependent on directed-bond order

entries.conventions: In this experiment Jxy−Jyx=2Dz, Dx and Dy are obtained by cyclic permutation; i and j are exchanged and D→−D is obtained.
entries.conditions: Bond-center inversion forces D=0. Absence of inversion only removes this prohibition; it does not guarantee nonzero D.

entries.title: Symmetric traceless exchange anisotropy
entries.definition: Subtract one third of the trace times the identity from the symmetric exchange tensor to obtain symmetric traceless anisotropy.
entries.conventions: J=J_iso I+Γ+A(D)，Γ=(J+Jᵀ)/2−Tr(J)I/3。
entries.conditions: Here Γ is an exchange matrix, not the Brillouin-zone center or lead broadening.

entries.title: axial vector transform of real spin
entries.definition: The real spin is transformed according to axial vector under spatial orthogonal operation. Mirror and inversion cannot apply the polar vector rule.

variables.meaning: axial vector matrix acting on spin components

entries.conventions: S→det(R)RS; physical spin is inversion even. Bond operations may additionally exchange sites.
entries.conditions: only applies to declared true spins; arbitrary orbital pseudospins require independent representation matrix .

entries.title: generator and the conserved quantity to be tested
entries.definition: Q is a Hermitian observation quantity; when it generates a continuous unitary transformation, the Hamiltonian symmetry can be tested through the commutator.

variables.unit: depends on the specific operator; the spin in this experiment is dimensionless

entries.conventions: U(θ)=exp(−iθQ); for Q without explicit time, closed system conservation requirement [H,Q]=0.
entries.conditions: The fact that the expected value of an initial state is exactly flat does not prove the conservation of the complete operator; open systems must check L†Q.

entries.title: Commutators and closed-system conservation
entries.definition: The commutator tests whether the continuous symmetry transformation is compatible with the Hamiltonian, and gives the operator for the change of the observed quantity of the closed system.

variables.meaning: An observable with no explicit time dependence

entries.conventions: d⟨Q⟩/dt=i⟨[H/ℏ,Q]⟩. Keep ℏ explicit rather than mixing energy and angular-frequency units by silently setting ℏ=1.
entries.conditions: This experiment reports on the Frobenius norm; the contributions of all operators must be added together before determining whether the sum is zero.

entries.title: Lindblad adjoint generator and conservation
entries.definition: Conservation in the complete open system is determined by the generator's adjoint action on observables.

variables.meaning: Jump operator with square root of rate

entries.conventions: L†Q=i[H/ℏ,Q]+Σ_c(C_c†QC_c−{C_c†C_c,Q}/2)。
entries.conditions: needs to check that the complete operator is zero; the Hamiltonian conservation quantity may be destroyed by dissipation, and the contributions of each channel may also cancel.

entries.title: Kramers protection diagnostics for finite spin systems
entries.definition: Check the square of antiunitary time reversal and Hamiltonian symmetry to establish Kramers protection conditions.
entries.conventions: In this experiment, the single spin 1/2 has T²=−I; the two spin 1/2 as a whole have T²=+I. change of basis is U_T′=U†U_TU*.
entries.conditions: Time reversal must also preserve the Hamiltonian. There is no lattice momentum here, so this is not a full-Brillouin-zone magnetic-space-group diagnostic.

entries.title: Character projection onto an isotypic component
entries.definition: Weight a group average by an irreducible character to extract every copy of that irreducible representation from the given space.

variables.meaning: Group matrix in the current orbital basis

entries.conventions: P_α=(d_α/|G|)Σ_g χ_α(g)^*D(g). Its trace equals the total dimension of that isotypic component.
entries.conditions: This experiment uses a four-orbital C₄ᵥ representation or two copies of it. Projection onto a repeated irreducible type does not automatically select an individual copy.

entries.title: Matrix element projection and partner function
entries.definition: uses irreducible representation matrix elements instead of character to construct mutually transformable partners within the same irreducible representation .

variables.meaning: Matrix element of the target irreducible representation

entries.conventions: P_mn=(d_α/|G|)Σ_g D^α_mn(g)^*D(g). Partner tags can only be interpreted given a reference representation and coordinate convention.
entries.conditions: Non-diagonal P_mn is generally not an orthogonal projection matrix; the internal change of basis of partner phases and equivalence bases do not change the representation space.

entries.title: unifies selection rule with actual matrix elements
entries.definition: Check whether the operator representation tensor the initial representation contains the final representation. Positive containment multiplicity means only that symmetry permits the transition.
entries.conventions: n_allowed=(1/|G|)Σ_g χ_f(g)^*χ_O(g)χ_i(g). The actual intensity is calculated from the square of the matrix element modulus of the specified operator.
entries.conditions: Polarization, actual wavefunctions, and reduced matrix elements can still make an allowed transition vanish. Finite-group containment multiplicities are not general SU(2) CG coefficients.

entries.title: Schur structure of repeated irreducible representations
entries.definition: When the same irreducible representation occurs multiple times, the symmetric Hamiltonian can mix copies, but must be compatible on the partner space with the representation.

variables.meaning: Hermitian matrix acting on equivalent copy space

entries.conventions: H_E=H_copy⊗I_partner adopts the base order of replica first and then partner.
entries.conditions: Two copies of E form a four-dimensional isotypic space, usually split into two doublets at different energies. The whole isotypic space is not automatically a protected fourfold degeneracy.

entries.title: wavevector Star and conjugate real mode
entries.definition: A wavevector star contains distinct arms generated by the parent point group modulo reciprocal-lattice vectors. A real field requires q and −q coefficients to be complex conjugates.

variables.meaning: Fractional wavevector in the parent reciprocal basis

entries.conventions: f(r)=Σ_j A_j cos(2πq_j·r+φ_j). Non-self-conjugate pairs give cos/sin; there is only one real mode for q≡−q.
entries.conditions: is currently a commensurability experiment for the known square scalar pattern, N=2/3/4, not an arbitrary three-dimensional space group representation database.

entries.title: translation stabilizer , supercell index and translation domain
entries.definition: The actual field-preserving translations form H∩T, with translational orbits of size equal to the index of this subgroup in the declared translational group.

variables.meaning: Declare the translation group in an N×N supercell
Stabilizer of the current pattern in the finite parent group

entries.conventions: N_translation=|T|/|H∩T|; the rectangular period L_x L_y can exceed this minimum translation index.
entries.conditions: All groups in this graph are finite periodic quotient groups. The index does not automatically specify a standard three-dimensional cell or establish the thermodynamic stability of a pattern.

entries.title: Fourier coefficients and satellite weights of a scalar modulation
entries.definition: Decompose the discrete real-space mode into complex coefficients on the reciprocal grid. Their squared magnitudes give the relative weights in this model.
entries.conventions: F(q)=N⁻²Σ_r f(r)exp(−2πiq·r)；I(q)=|F(q)|²；F(−q)=F(q)^*。
entries.conditions: Atomic scattering factors, displacement factors Q·u, and magnetic polarization are omitted. These weights cannot be used directly as experimental diffraction cross sections.

entries.title: Parseval inspection and phase prediction
entries.definition: Check normalization by equating the real-field mean square to the sum of all Fourier weights, distinguishing coefficient phases from intensities.

variables.meaning: declares the side length of supercell

entries.conventions: Σ_q|F(q)|²=N⁻²Σ_r|f(r)|². Mutually different q/−q each have A²/4 intensity, and the overall phase does not change them.
entries.conditions: The self-conjugate arm has only one real degree of freedom, and the phase is only multiplied by cosφ; the conclusion of two different satellites cannot be applied unconditionally.

entries.title: Bloch square relations for screws and glides
entries.definition: Repeating the half-translation operation produces a full lattice translation, together with the central sign of the single- or double-valued representation.

variables.meaning: Radian wave vector along the operation’s translation direction
Operation matrix in the periodic Bloch basis
Single value is 0, double value is 1/2

entries.conventions: G(k)²=(−1)^(2s)exp(−ik_x)I; k_x=2πf_x when entering reciprocal lattice fraction f_x.
entries.conditions: must first satisfy the little group condition that Rk−k is an integer reciprocal lattice . The model limits three-dimensional operations to a momentum line and does not cover the complete space group classification.

entries.title: Momentum-dependent glide or screw eigenvalues
entries.definition: eigenvalues are the two square roots of the square relationship; even if the matrix is strictly periodic, a single tag can be exchanged after traversing a reciprocal lattice period.
entries.conventions: Double value: g_±=±i exp(−ik_x/2); Single value: g_±=±exp(−ik_x/2).
entries.conditions: In the energy degenerate block, G should be re-diagonalized before reading the label; the energy basis vector arbitrarily selected by the numerical solver is not necessarily the G eigenstate.

entries.title: TRIM Kramers partner pairing at both ends
entries.definition: Antiunitary time reversal links k and −k. At TRIM, combine T²=−I with momentum-dependent operation labels to compare endpoint partner pairing.

variables.meaning: Momentum for which 2k is a reciprocal-lattice vector

entries.conventions: U_T H(k)^* U_T†=H(−k). In this model, the double-valued Γ-end partner labels are opposite and the X-end partner labels are the same.
entries.conditions: Partner switching requires G to preserve every momentum on the line, both ends to be TRIM, and both G and T to be symmetries. Overlapping bands alone do not prove protection.

entries.title: Anticommuting mass term that breaks a glide or screw
entries.definition: Add an anticommuting mass to the explicitly defined two- or four-band model to test which broken constraint can open the middle direct gap.

variables.meaning: Minimum middle direct gap over the full momentum line

entries.conventions: H_m=H₀+mτ_z⊗I; Δ_direct=2|m| in this model of b=0.
entries.conditions: This follows from the declared matrices and anticommutation relations, not a universal gap formula for screw-symmetric materials. A direct gap is neither an indirect gap nor a three-dimensional insulation criterion.
